column3: The Hebrew repeats generation and generation; BSB says all generations.
The Hebrew joins the mountains and Your bringing forth with and; BSB uses or.
The Hebrew names crushing; BSB specifies dust.
The Hebrew explicitly names yesterday and joins the night watch with and; BSB omits yesterday and uses or.
The Hebrew says they become sleep; BSB describes whisking them away in their sleep.
The Hebrew describes being cut down in the evening; BSB says fades.
The Hebrew says our hidden thing without explicitly adding sins and names Your face rather than presence.
The Hebrew describes the passing days and completed years with completed verbs; BSB has present verbs.
The Hebrew’s passing verb has a singular subject and flying is completed; BSB has they pass and we fly.
The Hebrew does not explicitly add You are due to the fear phrase as BSB does.
The Hebrew names sons rather than children and places splendor over them.
The Hebrew repeats the work of our hands and ends with establish it; BSB repeats the noun phrase as the final object.
